name: security-vpn-federation-session-review
intent: VPN gateway identity/posture mapping into tunnel and resource authority
artifacts: VPN/SP federation config, assertion validation, MFA assurance mapping and gateway session policies.
trace: Trace issuer authentication context into VPN authorization and session refresh/reconnect, including local fallback identities.
experiment: Using supplied gateway mappings or an owned gateway fixture, trace one synthetic federation identity and posture result into local VPN role, tunnel issuance and one permitted resource. Compare an assurance/posture mismatch or revoked reconnect under the actual profile.
disproof: A successful IdP login or missing UI MFA prompt does not prove gateway assurance downgrade; the assertion/session may already carry required assurance.
repair: Bind federation context and gateway session policy, verifying intended reconnect and required assurance.
branch_decisions: Map federated assertion assurance to the gateway session, device posture and resource policy. The IdP session and the VPN tunnel can have different documented lifetimes. A valid SSO response alone does not demonstrate internal network access; confirm only the owned permitted service path and classify revocation delay against the declared contract.
operational_method: Specialize in one supplied gateway/protocol profile: assertion/token validation, mapped local VPN role, device/posture identity, tunnel issuance and permitted resource ACL. Compare the IdP identity/assurance with the actual tunnel/session record and one owned service access result, including reassessment on reconnect or posture change where the contract requires it. A generic SAML fixture cannot define gateway enforcement; absent gateway mapping is an explicit blocker, not proof of internal access.
